title: A Flaw in ChatGPT’s Mac App Could Have Let Hackers Grab Sensitive Data
gist: Objective-See researchers found a now-patched flaw in OpenAI's macOS ChatGPT app that let local malware spoof trusted components and take over the app, exposing chat logs and connected browser sessions. Researcher Patrick Wardle argues AI companies' feature race leaves security an afterthought, and says more bugs are pending in ChatGPT's Dots integration.

insights.claim: A patched flaw in OpenAI's ChatGPT macOS app could have let an attacker with malware already on the machine take over ChatGPT, reading all chat logs and tapping connected sessions such as the browser.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: Concentrated chat history and permissions make AI apps a high-value target and a potential enterprise data-leak vector.
insights.locator: The bug could have been exploited

insights.claim: The exploit defeated three-layer signature checks by spawning a trusted script interpreter three times so the parent and grandparent checks passed, and the proof of concept needed about a dozen lines of code.
insights.speaker: Patrick Wardle
insights.so_what: Defence-in-depth via process-ancestry checks fails when any trusted helper accepts untrusted input.
insights.quote: the malicious script just spawns the script interpreter three times and then makes the request so it will satisfy the requirements

insights.claim: The attacker could also make ChatGPT run commands, such as accessing a browser or other sensitive applications, with requests appearing as legitimate instructions from OpenAI software.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: Agentic AI turns a local compromise into confused-deputy privilege escalation across other apps.

insights.claim: OpenAI acknowledged the flaw and fix in its change log on September 25, with a spokesperson saying it recognizes a need to move faster on security.
insights.speaker: Shane Bauer, OpenAI spokesperson
insights.so_what: OpenAI's public admission of a need for speed signals security debt amid fast product expansion.
insights.quote: We continue to evolve our security practices, but recognize a need to move faster

insights.claim: AI agents need broad system access like a building manager holding all room keys, so subverting them gives unprivileged code access to everything the agent can reach.
insights.speaker: Patrick Wardle
insights.so_what: Agent privileges concentrate risk, favouring endpoint-security and identity vendors that can govern agent access.
insights.quote: They are like the building manager who has access to the keys to all the rooms.

insights.claim: AI companies are fixated on adding features, and more features mean a broader attack surface, yet security still often seems an afterthought.
insights.speaker: Patrick Wardle
insights.so_what: Expect a continued stream of AI-app CVEs and rising security spend as AI products proliferate.
insights.quote: AI companies are fixated on adding features right now

insights.claim: Wardle also found a now-patched flaw in the dictation feature of Meta's Muse AI assistant that exposed an authentication token, and has submitted a new report on the integration between ChatGPT and OpenAI's always-on Dots assistant.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: Vulnerabilities cluster across vendors, so a pending OpenAI Dots bug is a near-term disclosure risk.
